A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same R2D2 research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original R2D2 results on WebArena, component ablations, manual error analysis, and qualitative task outcomes.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical evaluations and additionally reports an online-action efficiency comparison in Table 2.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain replay-buffer search, trajectory reflection, memory updates, and retrieval. Changing A* from 'breadth-first' to 'best-first' corrects its description. Appendix D newly describes buffer eviction but does not establish a change to the implemented method.

E1.justification: Both versions use WebArena's 812 queries covering CMS, Reddit, Shopping, Map, and GitLab, with English-only experiments. The added efficiency comparison introduces no new dataset, domain, or task scenario.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains ReACT, Tree-Search, AutoEval, LATS, AR, and BrowserGym; the reflection comparisons retain AR and LATS. The new efficiency table reuses Tree-Search and AutoEval without introducing a new comparison method.

E3.justification: New Section 4.4 evaluates average online actions needed to complete tasks, adding an efficiency metric alongside success rate. Existing benchmark settings and the 60-query error inspection are retained. Newly stated offline construction details do not establish revisions to previous experimental settings.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 adds an analysis testing whether R2D2 reduces live-environment interactions relative to Tree-Search and AutoEval. Existing episode, component, and failed-trajectory ablations, error analyses, and appendix case studies remain; shortening the main qualitative discussion does not remove those cases.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The retained episode curves show sequential performance development, not newly reported uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes R2D2's Map score from 29.6% to 28% and total success rate from 27.5% to 27.3%; most other changed entries are equivalent rounding. The successful-only ablation remains 20.5%, while its stated gap changes from 7.5 to 6.8 percentage points. New Table 2 reports 13.1 online steps for R2D2, 33.8 for Tree-Search, and 29.2 for AutoEval.

T1.justification: New Appendix D asserts O(1) replay-buffer space using bounded capacity and eviction, and O(N log N) search time using a priority queue. These brief complexity arguments have no counterpart in v1; existing mathematical definitions and algorithmic equations remain.

C1.justification: The central Remember/Reflect contribution and headline claims of 50% fewer navigation errors, threefold task completion, and a 17% advantage over prior methods are retained. The efficiency evidence supports an existing computational-overhead claim, while the revised title and acronym expansion do not redefine the contribution.

C2.justification: v2 expands the English-only limitation to discuss reliance on WebArena and GPT-4o, experimentation costs, and uncertain broader applicability. Section 4.4 and Appendix D additionally interpret fewer online actions as reduced latency and argue that LLM overhead is small. Existing failure interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly reports at most five offline construction actions per task, rule-based replay-buffer creation, capacity-limiting eviction, and approximately $200 in GPT-4o usage per WebArena pass. The GPT-4o specification, retriv framework, MiniLM embedding model, and appendix prompts are retained.

R1.justification: The Liu et al. (2024) reference changes from AutoDAN-Turbo to the distinct AutoDAN paper. Most other bibliography revisions update the same works, including identifying the previously anonymous webpage-UI paper as Liu et al. (2025). The broader research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v2 revises the title and acronym expansion, corrects grammar and terminology, condenses the results discussion, and moves navigation-failure introductory text into Section 3.2. It replaces the standalone main-text qualitative section with an appendix pointer and adds efficiency headings and acknowledgments. Most prose and organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn with heavier arrows and revised styling. An efficiency table is added, while the original qualitative Table 2 becomes Table 3 on a separate page and prompt placement changes. The architecture diagram, empirical plots, and prompt images are retained.

improvement.justification: The new action-count comparison provides limited empirical support for the existing efficiency argument, while expanded limitations and implementation disclosures make the work easier to assess. Terminology and ablation arithmetic also improve. These gains remain modest: elapsed time is not measured, and Appendix D provides only brief support for its complexity and latency assertions.
